I'm slightly thrown because I'm looking at the transcript where it's referred to as tab 110 in the presentation binder and then as master tab 389, but when I go to master tab 389, I find something completely different. So if you'll give me one moment, I'm sure we can sort this out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is 1 --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Reasonably short we can short it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is what the cover page says as well, binder 11, tab 389.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, I see what's happened, Your Honour. It's that the binder which I very kindly have been allowed to borrow for immediate use from this shelf has actually had this particular item removed, and perhaps that's because you've got it, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I've got Mr. Hannis's copy as it's annotated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't know who has the one that's come out of this bundle. But, Your Honours, with respect, I can probably manage with the references.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The particular passage you talk about, Dr. Karadzic saying: "The deputies are members of the supreme organ of authority, the Assembly. Now they must literally stay with the presidents of the municipalities." But in order to -- did you have some other part of what Dr. Karadzic says on that occasion in mind as demonstrating the point which you were apparently seeking to make?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those two sentences and then the next one that's highlighted --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Is that up on our screen now?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We do not need that" -- saying -- to give the entire passage. "A municipality president is basically the one who should be obeyed; that is the way it must be. We know our deputies and we can be sure they are very serious-minded people. None of them is power-loving and would mistreat a president of a municipality or undermine his authority. We do not need that because the president of the municipality is the one who carries out our plans."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You see so when you gave your answer a few minutes ago -- this is your answer, 44, line 1. Page 44 line 1: "When Karadzic describes the assemblies as a supreme organ, he then goes on to discuss how the assemblymen should go to the municipalities and sit with the presidents of municipalities and carry out, implement the policies of the Assembly. That is the context of Karadzic's reference." Now, you see, what I'm putting to you is that, Ms. Hanson, that precisely misstates both the correct position and what Dr. Karadzic is saying because he is precisely not saying, You go out there and implement the policies of the Assembly. What he's saying is: You sit down with the people who live there, you sit down with the people that work there, you talk to them, you listen to them, and they do what they have to do in their locality. Do you accept my summary as I've just put it to you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because he says: "The president of the municipality is the one who carries out our plans."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, we're going to go endlessly around in circles. This is precisely what I'm putting to you, that whereas your answer talked about the assemblymen going out to implement the policies of the Assembly. What's being talked about very specifically by Dr. Karadzic is, it's the president of the municipality who does the implementation. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is saying that the president of the municipality does the implementation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. And very specifically in the sentence before he says that: "Our deputies, serious-minded people, they would not undermine the authority of the president of a municipality, doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, from what you've seen of all the Assembly sessions and you've seen a lot and you've read -- I take it, Ms. Hanson, at some point you've read all the transcripts of all the Assembly sessions which you've mentioned in the course of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I read the passages identified by -- as a -- identify -- identified those passages where the speaker is known to be a member of a Crisis Staff, and I read their speech -- or a commissioner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or other parts that were relevant. But I did not read every Assembly session beginning to end.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So somebody else made a prior selection of relevance, did they, before you got down to reading those relevant passages?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone else identified every speaker, and on the basis of that list of who's speaking at what time, I went to the Assembly sessions -- to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the relevant parts of the Assembly sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Are you able to say then from what you have read whether it was the general practice for deputies to report in Assembly sessions on -- well, ranges of specific local issues from their constituencies?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the passages I mention -- of the passages that I looked at in detail, that was one of what they -- one of their topics that they talked about was reporting on issues of importance from their municipality. They also discussed the laws under consideration. There were other topics of discussion as well. As I say, I'm not going to speak about the part that I did not -- the parts that I did not look at in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, if I put a proposition to you, then you can either say that you don't know from the reading you've done or answer it as best you can. But what we actually see in this Bosnian Serb Assembly is, once again, something not unusual as far as parliaments are concerned. Deputies, Members of Parliament, will raise issues of policy concern, of major concern, they will use particular local issues to illustrate their points, they may raise from time to time particular local matters of special importance, but the tolerance of their colleagues for listening to any detailed accounts of their own problems in their own constituencies will have its limits because it is not a forum for reporting in detail by deputies on what's happening in their locality. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only answer on the basis of what I read from the Assembly sessions, and in there I see they do report on the municipalities, and I do not see evidence of other deputies saying, Enough already, we don't want to hear about that. So on the basis of what I said, I can't entirely agree with your proposition.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: How many municipalities were represented in the Bosnian Serb Assembly, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number. Not everyone, simply because of the structure of elections to the Bosnian republican parliament chambers, which then obviously created who were the deputies for the Bosnian Serb Assembly. So not every municipality, but certainly every -- from all regions of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's a point at which Your Honours can read the transcripts of the Assembly sessions and so the picture of the debate is one that Your Honours can get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We certainly can, Mr. Stewart, and the Chamber notices that now and then the interpretation of those words is not the same between Defence and the expert. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But, Your Honour, I'm trying, although the line is sometimes a difficult one, of course I'm trying to avoid simply taking cross-examination time in what's actually a debate or an argument about interpretation. The time for that sort of thing will come later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- Ms. Hanson, you have not seen any written reports by individual deputies to the Speaker or President of the Assembly, Mr. Krajisnik, in relation to the work of Crisis Staffs, have you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Or in fact of Mr. Krajisnik in any capacity?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have the written report of the work of the Novo Sarajevo Crisis Staff, which we saw was -- oh, forgive me, that was a government session. No, I have not seen written reports to Mr. Krajisnik on the work of Crisis Staffs, although we do see that the -- there is a National Security Council at the end of April reviewed a report on the work of Crisis Staffs, but I have not seen a written version of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you've not seen any -- well, to qualify this, apart from the major documents that are being looked at, the instructions given -- those by the government in April 1992 and then the December 1991 document, but you have not seen, have you, any written directives coming from the Assembly to Crisis Staffs, have you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No written directives, although I have indicated the instructions to Crisis Staffs in the -- spoken in the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I just want to move on now to a different point which arises out of paragraph 45 of your report which concerns the military role of Crisis Staffs. And then where it starts at that point and then I want to pick the matter up at the end of paragraph 46 where you have a sentence: "The Kljuc Crisis Staff claimed that no significant and important questions from the military and police domain were resolved without the Crisis Staff." And then in the footnote that quote is expanded a bit. There is a general question here, a point I've noticed, Ms. Hanson. The translations which appear in your footnotes are in many, if not practically all cases, different from the translations we have. Is this because you did your own translations as you went along from the B/C/S documents that you were working from?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In some cases the English translation had not yet been made; in others, I didn't consult it at all because I worked primarily with the B/C/S original documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In this particular item which I wonder if you could have is presentation binder 7 at tab 245 according to my note. It's also master binder 4 at 148, if that's more convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the B/C/S on the computer evidence and could we have the translation on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I brought the first four binder but not number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, the passage that I'm looking for here, Ms. Hanson, is at page 3 of the translation. I'm sorry I can't help you immediately where it is in B/C/S, but it's not a very long document.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're still trying to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And it's a sentence which in the English translation -- it's a bit in your footnote that you start off the translation as: "VRS commanders," and in the translation we have the paragraph begins: "Throughout the armed conflict." Do you see that? You probably have the B/C/S --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the presentation tab 245 is not the work of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I'm so sorry. It's probably better then if we do master binder 4, tab 148. That's -- my apologies. I'm confident about the master binder reference.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's presentation tab 243, if I may use, because we have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, yeah. I thought that's what I said, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, because in the transcript it said 245.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, in fact, you're quite right, Ms. Hanson. I had corrected an earlier note somewhere else and I read the earlier one. So it's 243. Presentation binder 6, 243. And 4, 148 as well.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just finding the exact B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, my apologies, it's not simple incompetence on my part; it's complicated incompetence because of the changing of numbering as we've been going along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one thought about incompetence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one thought about incompetence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the first paragraph on the B/C/S page 00349534.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So anyway, it's -- well, either translation. But the -- your -- I'll read from the translation in the binder: "Throughout the armed conflict representatives (commanders) of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina regularly participated in sessions of the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency. These representatives were in command of and conducted combat activities to defend the territory and citizens of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly against Muslim extremists and maintained good cooperation with the Crisis Staff of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly. All questions related to the army and police were resolved within the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly." Now, first of all, Ms. Hanson, I entirely accept that your translation can perfectly legitimately be different in the sense that it's actually ordered differently -- that those sentences can be -- two translations can structure the translation in a different way, and that's what's happened. But somewhere along the line that passage which appears in the binder translation "these representatives were in command or then conducted combat activities to defend the territory and citizens of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly against Muslim extremists" seems to have got lost. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My footnote references are intended to summarise the information that I drew from the original document and to point the reader to which part of the document. I agree, this is a -- in the nature just of a summary and parts of that section were left out. And in that respect, the quotation marks are not warranted in that it's not a completely one-for-one translation, but it summarised what I wanted the reader to look for in the original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, I think that perhaps that occurred, it happens in a number of other cases, you appear to be perfectly straightforwardly accepting that where something appears in quotation marks it ought to embrace everything that falls between the beginning and end of those quotation marks.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where there are not quotation marks, yes, I'm generally summarising; where there are quotation marks, it is my translation of the B/C/S or if I did consult the English translation -- it is intended to be more a word for word -- a literal excerpt. However, I cannot claim that in the final polishing I went through and checked everything that is in quotation marks. So some summaries have apparently entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's not a completely trivial point here, is it, anyway because what's got lost is that these representatives of the VRS were in command of and conducted combat activities is making it very plain, isn't it, that as far as the military responsibilities, the actions are concerned, it is they who are in control and command?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is clearly stated in this passage. How -- I would simply note that I cite this passage in support of the statement regarding the commmonality of purpose, not of the military command of the Kljuc Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm just tracking down my reference here. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: At --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Apologies for the pause, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Paragraph 50, you report, last sentence it begins on 23, it's the last line on 23: "In other cases" -- I beg your pardon, it's the previous sentence. "In a few cases", that three lines up, it's a few lines up on the bottom of page 23. "In a few cases the heads of the Crisis Staffs styled themselves commanders and took their control over local forces to the point of assuming direct command of local units." And you give a number of examples and I'm not going to grind through them all, Ms. Hanson, but I am going to take you to one which is Ilijas, that's over the page at footnote 86, page 24, you say: "Ilijas" the footnote says, "Ratko Adzic was president of the Crisis Staff and called himself the commander of VSN BiH Ilijas." And VSN is just VRS proper. A different time when the terminology was slightly different.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my understanding of VSN.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then you've got letter from Adzic to the president of Presidency. And you dealt with this matter on Thursday, the 3rd of March, in your evidence. It starts at page 11. You refer to the letter and then you say: "So we" -- page 12 of the transcript it was, line 3. It's a short passage, Ms. Hanson. "We see here that Ratko Adzic is also the president. He's also the president of the Crisis Staff of Ilijas. We see him here calling himself commander of the army and requesting tanks and aircraft guns for clearing the municipality." Do you know what Mr. Ratko Adzic's position was in the army before the date of this particular letter?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you know that he was in fact a general or at least -- I understand general, but at least a senior -- a very senior officer in the army?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And that the -- so you don't know that the reason why Mr. Adzic would have called himself commander of the army in that particular place is because he was?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I'm not saying that he wasn't. Saying that he is president of the Ilijas Crisis Staff which -- the transcript doesn't indicate -- I was saying we see, it was kind of an elliptical comment in ellipsis. He is otherwise president of the Ilijas Crisis Staff. We don't see-- we couldn't really see it in that document, but that this document, the president of the Crisis Staff uses a military term "commander" -- calls himself commander, was commander. I'm simply referring to the terms of that letter, that he was a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Hanson, I put it to you, that's not good enough. There are, and I want to clear away any battle lines that don't exist, but there are cases of people styling themselves commanders, there are cases of people strutting around in uniforms with weapons because the opportunity to be soldiers has been presented to them. But you give this as an example supporting the text. And the text is: "In a few cases the heads of the Crisis Staffs styled themselves commanders and took their control over local forces to the point of assuming direct command of local units." And I'm suggesting to you that it's utterly inappropriate to use as a support for that text somebody who was styling himself the commander because he was, because he was, a senior officer in the army and took his control over local forces to the point of assuming direct command of local units because he was the commander of the local units and he would have been signaling failing in his duty if he hadn't actually performed his function as a senior officer of the army. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have the translation on the ELMO, because I see that we have the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I qualify that sentence to include those cases where they called themselves commanders, but certainly I will -- I was not aware of Adzic's position in the army or that the exact nature of the units under his control, but I will gladly accept that that is -- if that is the case that he is calling himself commander because he is commander and is commanding units. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In the same way that General Eisenhower styled himself commander and chief of the allied forces in Europe because he was?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had, I imagine, an appointment, a commission, to that position. I don't know the nature of Avdic's position at that point. I do not know enough about -- I don't know anything about his previous military position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I should say, out of respect to General Eisenhower, I don't think he was the supreme commander was probably the phrase. Ms. Hanson --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask, Mr. Stewart, it's not entirely clear to me. I tried to fully understand. Mr. Adzic was appointed in the VSN BiH and by whom because that question is based upon he being the commander of that army and it's not entirely clear. And since Ms. Hanson says he doesn't know of his position --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not in a -- I'm not in a position to give the details of the history of his commissions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But if you include it in your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm trying to answer Your Honour's question. My instructions are, I can't give you more specific detail, that he had been a professional soldier and he didn't suddenly become an officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I do understand that. I fully understand and you make comparison with General Eisenhower. Of course I do agree that I know his position and he was a general, but that doesn't make him automatically, for example, the commander in chief of the Madurodam forces. That's -- I'm trying to find out what exactly we are talking about. I think I'm not at this moment disputing, apart from that it's not for me to dispute, it's just for me to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I try to understand whether he was just a general before and now is a general in a force which is not entirely familiar to me, the Ilijas Serbian army command, and at the bottom it says the Ilijas VSN BiH. I don't know who is responsible for appointing people in that army and whether his appointment as a general prior to acting in this formation had any relation with this specific function. So I'm trying to find out -- he was a general so he now says, now I'm a commander. It's not uncommon for generals to say, I'm in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out and trying to understand both your question and the answers and I'm trying to find out whether your question includes that since he was appointed - and then of course I'd like to know by whom - commander of the Ilijas VSN BiH or that he was -- well, let's say a general in the JNA before and suddenly appears, I'm saying "appears" as a very neutral term, as commander of the Ilijas VSN BiH, in order to both understand the answers and your questions, I need more than just, He was a general so he appears now here as a general. I do need this information as well in order to understand and to assess whether the report of Ms. Hanson in this respect shows any shortcomings, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, may I do it this way, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I 100 per cent accept what Your Honour has said in the sense that the Trial Chamber needs this material to assess Ms. Hanson's report. With respect, Your Honours don't necessarily need all that material now. Some evidence from the Defence would give Your Honour those details, and I'm -- without taking a lot of time or instructions from Mr. Krajisnik and researching, I can't give Your Honour the details. The point -- just so that Your Honour can fairly understand the question and the answer at the moment, the point I'm essentially putting to Ms. Hanson is that there was no question of Mr. Adzic just self-styling himself, calling himself something he wasn't, that what he is calling himself in this document is what he actually legitimately was, as -- Judge Hanoteau has a question I see, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, in the document that we have in front of us on the screen, Mr. Ratko Adzic calls himself commander of the Ilijas VSN BiH. In your footnote you also say that he also is or was president of the Crisis Staff. Right? My question: So in a way he accumulated two titles, two functions. In this kind of request or demand that emanated from the Crisis Staff and was addressed to the Presidency, was it usual that the president of the Crisis Staff as another title to his own, even if his title is legitimate? Are there any other cases in which he uses both titles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not -- I do not recall any other document from Ratko Adzic in which he uses both titles. He does sign some documents or uses the title "president of the Crisis Staff" in some, and in this document "commander." I have not seen any from him in which he uses both, nor do I recall at the moment any other Crisis Staff presidents using a title -- using two titles in such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have to interpret this assertion of a military title as being a militarisation of the Crisis Staff, meaning that the Crisis Staff is playing an essential part in coordinating military action? Could this have that kind of meaning for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very much so. I cite this in my report as an example of those places where the overlap at the level of the Crisis Staff was almost complete, where the president of the Crisis Staff was a commander or called himself a commander signs here, signs as commander, is a commander. An example of where the Crisis Staff had, as I said, almost complete overlap with the military command roles, I suggest this is the most extreme end of what I call the spectrum, and we do not see this everywhere. But when you have one and the same person as president of the Crisis Staff and as an army commander, you see the strongest example of the militarisation of the Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, one last question as to the addressee of this letter. Who was this letter addressed to in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic was the president of the Presidency at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, when you say in response to His Honour Judge Hanoteau's question: "When you have one and the same person as president of the Crisis Staff and as an army commander, you see the strongest example of the militarisation of the Crisis Staffs," I put it to you that actually in the case of Mr. Adzic it's precisely because he is properly performing his duties as an army officer that he writes this letter in these terms and signs it in that capacity because it is very specifically relating to a military matter.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this letter is a military matter. He signs it as a military commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In fact, as your report recognises, there's a -- there's a huge range of -- a huge range of relationships between Crisis Staff and military, isn't there, at this time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That in some cases the military just get on with their job as soldiers, in some cases the Crisis Staff, perhaps because there isn't such a military strength, the Crisis Staff kit themselves out in uniforms, get their weapons, and regard themselves as the soldiers. That's right, isn't it, as a picture of the range and variation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. The only reference I have of Crisis Staffs kitting themselves out in uniforms and getting their weapons is in Kljuc where they have this decision to allow themselves to wear uniforms and carry weapons. When I'm saying -- not that the Crisis Staff themselves are the soldiers, but in some places we see the Crisis Staffs establishing local units and arming them and in some places issuing them orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Hanson, I want to move on to look at these various documents, including the one which -- you have not generally used that particular label, but it's been used often Variants A and B, it's been often used in this trial and in other trials. The -- can we take, please, the -- you told the Trial Chamber I think that as far as you were concerned the best version of this -- that document the -- well, no, let's start somewhere else, please, first. Master binder 1, tab 21. Now, this was the recommendation dated the 11th of December, 1991, emanating from the 3rd Assembly Session of the Bosnian Serb Assembly. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And it recommends -- this is just a recap because you've given evidence about this, Ms. Hanson, recommends to the Deputies' Club those assemblies where the rule of majority vote is used to impose decisions that run counter of the interests of the Serb people to take appropriate decisions on the establishment of municipal assemblies of the Serbian people. So, rephrasing that, that's -- that's municipalities where it's the Muslims because they're the national group in question. The Muslims are in control?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: And/or the Croats. It doesn't specify Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's absolutely right, Ms. Hanson. But for practical purposes in most cases we're talking about Muslim control.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were also municipalities where the Croats were the majority.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the most important thing is that for non-Serbian majority.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Non-Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And this is -- there's nothing secret about this document. It's -- and there's no ambiguity about its source, is there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And in fact there isn't any ambiguity about where it's going or to whom it's addressed, is there?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That all seems clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That all seems very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Then when we get to the document Variant A and B -- we can stay with the same binder, I appreciate you don't have the actual binder. But the document is tab 23 in the same binder, master binder 1. And I'm taking that because I think you referred to this document as the most complete version of --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's one passage that in some translations is rendered as illegible but not in this one so I find it the best --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's the best working tool.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- first of all, from your perusal of all the documentation in this case, can you offer an explanation of why this document says: "Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina Main Board" on the cover sheet and is then typed -- signed at the end "SDS Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as to why it says "Main Board" we know the Main Board existed; we know its role in the SDS. We know there was a meeting of the Main Board on the 20th of December. As for the SDS Crisis Staff, we do see reference to SDS Crisis Staffs or -- I'm sorry, an SDS Crisis Staff at the republican level. We see a -- references in March during the barricades. Karadzic also as early as the summer of 1991 says in an intercept, We have a Crisis Staff here. He seems to be referring to the republic level of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Have you seen documentation relating -- apart from just what you've just mentioned, have you seen documentation relating to the SDS republican level Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have mentioned now the references. Those are the references I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's all?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Are there documents that tell you and through you the Trial Chamber the membership of that Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The March references there are also -- now that I say -- I believe intercept references to the March Crisis Staff, but since that was March and I think in the context appears to be related to the barricade -- the question of the barricades in Sarajevo, I couldn't even say it's the same as this. So I believe in those intercepts Rajko Dukic is mentioned in that intercept, but I can't with any certainty connect that to this typed-signed Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: What was your reaction when you first saw on this document that it said "Main Board" on the cover sheet and different organ, SDS Crisis Staff, at the end of the document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall my original reaction, but I --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Was it --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- do not see them as necessarily mutually incompatible in that we see -- at the republic -- in the municipal level we see Crisis Staffs formed within the municipal boards. So it is -- it certainly struck me that there is no other reference at this time to an SDS Crisis Staff. Yes, that struck me. But the front page reference to the Main Board -- it didn't strike me as -- necessarily, as I say, in conflict with the front page description of the Main Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's odd, though, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is anomalous in that there are no other references at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's odd. Ms. Hanson, it's simply odd, isn't it, to have one organ referred to on the cover sheet of the document and then an apparently different organ to having its title, name, at the end, as the -- in some sense the signatory. It is odd, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's unusual, yes. Odd, anomalous.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, unusual, odd. I'm not going to quibble about three syllables or one, Ms. Hanson. So my question following from that then is: Isn't it obviously sufficiently odd to cry out for further inquiry and as much inquiry as can reasonably be carried out into explaining that discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question of a Crisis Staff in December is sufficiently odd. We have looked for reference -- I know other people in my section have -- we have discussed, what is this Crisis Staff? We have looked for other references. That's how I am aware of the other references I have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It sounds as if you haven't quite come up with an answer.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when one doesn't receive positive identification, we can't say -- no other Crisis Staff -- no such republican level Crisis Staff at this time has been found, so no, yet -- there have been no yet -- until as far as this date no other citings of this. So it's negative results. I can't prove a negative. Nothing else has been found.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Just it may be in passing, it may not, it depends. But the very last sheet, page, in the B/C/S section of this tab is a page of handwritten -- not a photocopy of the page, of handwritten material. Can you cast any light on that, who wrote it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who wrote it. It would appear to be an indication of the distribution of this --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, we've got the translation, so we see 93A.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 93A, 93B. The -- there's a reference to Mico, perhaps Stanisic. And under 93C, Banja Luka Stojan, also to Gorazde Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, we see that -- I'm sorry, I don't want to stop you from answering the question, Ms. Hanson. I'm not asking you to go through the content. Can I, though, ask you this: Have you any idea of the date of this document? The page, I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My -- I have not consulted the original in the vault, but the fact that it was stamped together suggests to me that it was written on the back page of the document or on something attached to it. And as for the date of the drawing -- the date of the writing, I can't say anything more about it than -- we only have what's there. There's nothing else to date it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's not even clear whether it was written in 1991 or 1992 or as opposed to later, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, microphone please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you for the reminder.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There's one that might date. It says: "Assembly tomorrow." "Recognition of Krajina regions have been proclaimed in the Assembly," so those are consistent with shortly after the time of this issuing wouldn't not appear to be referring to anything after 1992, but there's certainly nothing -- no date given in the writing or anything to indicate exactly when it was written.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- you have said that there was a meeting of the SDS Main Board on the 20th of December, 1991. Can we look, please, at -- it's presentation binder item 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, if you could find a moment a little bit earlier than usual, that means not later than within the next five minutes to have the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, actually, Your Honour, now wouldn't be a bad moment because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- this particular document which has been a horrendous one to identify, I wouldn't mind sorting that out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll have the short break now and we'll resume just after 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, so far as -- and whichever particular version of this document, the instructions Variants A and B that we're talking about, you, I take it, have no reliable idea of when and how it was prepared?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Or indeed by whom?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of a letter from the SDS in response, I believe, to a request for information which stated that this was -- the document was written by -- I believe it says a group of retired JNA officers. However, the rest of that letter -- the claim that the SDS knows nothing more about the document I find contradicted by the evidence I have seen. So I do not give that letter much credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The -- your position that there was an SDS Main Board meeting on the 20th of December, 1991, that's placed on the -- the diary of Mr. Grkovic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Could we look at that item, please. It's actually in master binder 9 at tab 372 -- 372.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For those that not yet on the master level --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For those not on the master level, what would be the presentation number?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So sorry, Your Honour. It's presentation binder -- it's tab 12. In fact, I'm -- the master binder that I have for this goes backwards, so it looks it's if -- rather than being 372, it's actually 374. I naively thought that the tab before 373 would be 372, but call we old-fashioned. It's actually -- I think it's master binder 374.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But anyway, I see you're looking at the B/C/S version of that document, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It actually shows, doesn't it, at the top of -- I'm reading from the translation, but -- the English translation in the bundle, but you can perhaps confirm that it matches. It's got handwritten Friday, 20th December, 1991, at the top. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then underneath: "1600 meeting at the Main Board in the Deputies' Club." Is that a correct translation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then at the very bottom there's a sort of interjection which is shown in a box in the translation under the heading 19th of December, 1991, and then a number of -- well, dashed or bullet-point type items. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then at the very bottom of the page in the English translation - it may not be at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S - it says again: "1600 Main Board."

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then -- it's over the page in the English translation, wherever exactly it is in the B/C/S, it says: "For Monday at 1800 and GO," that's Main Board, "and Deputies' Club of SDS Sarajevo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that in the B/C/S. It's not on that page in the B/C/S nor do we seem to have that page of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the general recollection, but I do not have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You'll need the next page which I'll endeavour to get for you straight away. Yes, you need the next page. I have to ask this back, Ms. Hanson, because I've borrowed this binder from the registry at the moment. It's SA 043906 is the reference number it bears at the tope. I promise Ms. Philpott I'm going to make sure the this piece of paper gets back in her binder. Is that correct, that that's now continued?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: For Monday, at 6.00, Main Board and Deputies' Club SDS Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, all I'm going to put to you is that you yourself don't know whether there was a meeting of the 20th or on the 23rd or both or, in theory, neither?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the basis of my saying that there was a meeting of the Main Board on the 20th. This document is the basis for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. So where we see that -- because we now see that there is an entry of there being a meeting arranged apparently at 4.00 on Friday, the 20th, and 4.00 -- 6.00, I beg your pardon, on the Monday, the 23rd. You -- I'm slightly repeating myself -- you simply don't know whether there was two meetings or whether there was a replacement on the meeting on the Monday for one that was postponed on the Friday. You just don't know?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, you say something about the 23rd. I'm not able to follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I had understood that Friday, the 20th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then on the next page of the English translation for Monday at 1800, Monday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I have no -- in the tab you gave us, I do not have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, Your Honour, I'm so sorry. That was the page that the witness sought. It -- I suspect what's happened is that it's not got into the presentation binder, but it is in the main binder only. I see Mr. Hannis nodding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look then at the translation because --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the same may apply that it's only in the master binder. Your Honour, shall I hand this up to the one to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you can do that without war with Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: She's been extremely tolerant so far, Your Honour. She'll give me another sticker to make sure that the place is not lost, but this time I can stick it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you need this one from me? You don't. Thank you so much. Yes, so at the top there we see for Monday, Ms. Hanson. I'd added on the 23rd --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, on an assumption which I had made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Please tell me if it would be unwarranted, Ms. Hanson, that the Friday as the 20th and then it's the same Monday that the writer is likely to be talking about following that Friday?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that seems likely. Because we see also on that page Saturday -- there was an Assembly session on the 21st, and then it says Sunday, 22nd. So it seems logical that Monday is the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't want to dwell on this too long. Ms. Hanson, it's just this, isn't it: That you do only know about these meetings and dates of these meetings from these pieces of paper?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have the minutes of the Bratunac Municipal Board on the 23rd of December distributing material entirely consistent with the 19 December instructions, saying it came from a meeting of the SDS -- I believe he uses the word "Presidency." So I would say there was a meeting by the evening of the 23rd of December. That is another indication of a meeting at this time, but it's not specifically the Main Board on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But if the Bratunac document is an accurate report, it signifies, or it shows that the document came into Bratunac hands earlier than the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the evening of the 23rd, at which point Deronjic is sharing it with the rest of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Hanson, I understand what you're saying. You're saying that the document can't have fallen into their hands at a meeting at 6.00 on Monday because that would have been too late.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to check the time of the meeting in Bratunac, but my inclination is to say it wasn't -- it couldn't get from Sarajevo to Bratunac that evening all in one. So my inclination is to say it was before the evening of the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Understood. The -- well, then -- that's the date of the meeting. So far as the -- your report is concerned, paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm putting intact -- and it is intact I think, isn't it? I'll do that later, Ms. Philpott.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Paragraph 15 of your report -- I'm sorry, 14. You say that: "The 19th of December, 1991, instructions set out the preparations in two distinct stages for the takeover of power at the grass roots level and the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines." And I'm just inviting you, and let's look at that master binder tab 1, item 23, just inviting you to indicate where that document shows that it was preparations for the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic -- I'm sorry, I've walked away from the microphone. Where it shows that it was preparation for the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is instructing the SDS to form municipal organs for the Serbian people, to mobilise and create a Serbian police reserve and to then take over power in the municipality in Variant A or, in those areas where Serbs were a majority, in Variant B. And the sum total of those actions is creating separate municipalities, separate municipal authorities on ethnic lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, it is a leap from what this document says to the proposition that it was preparation for the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that dividing municipalities along ethnic lines is the intention of this document. It was distributed, as we know, widely, so such divisions would take place throughout Bosnia at the municipal level according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Does it -- where does it refer in this document to the division of the municipalities in terms of territory, population?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under Variant B where it says these measures are to be taken -- implemented in those areas where Serbs are a majority, that's in the first section, item 3 on the first page --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say A or B?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the very first section before Variant A.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. In the introduction?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the introduction. Under item 3 it says: "These tasks, measures, and activities are to be carried out throughout the territory of the socialist republic, completely in municipalities where the Serbs are a majority and partially where the Serbs are in a minority." And under Variant B it indicates that certain measures are to be taken out -- taken -- are to be implemented in those places. Territorial I would assume where Serbs are the majority in terms of the food reserves and of the stockpiles and the security. Overall the division is in the municipal government dividing the municipality along ethnic lines and that the Serbs are setting up their own municipal organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So when you talk about the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines, you're talking about politically and organised in government and local government terms, are you?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: And within the municipalities. We see in the Variant B municipalities an actual division of the territory in that some parts of the municipality would be declared the Serbian municipality. We see actual agreements on the territorial or proposed -- I'm sorry, not agreements, but proposals for division of the municipalities proposed by the SDS on the actual territory, naming which streets would be divided. We don't see that in this document, but we see in the declaration of Serbian municipalities in Variant B municipalities, that some territory is declared as belonging to the Serb municipality and other parts of that municipality are not. So it is also a territorial division.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, this is not, I assure the Trial Chamber, an area of major exploration for purposes of this case for the purposes of this case. But have you in the course of your work on Crisis Staffs for the purposes of this report and more widely as you have described it to the Trial Chamber, have you also examined and considered any material in relation to the establishment of Crisis Staffs by the Muslim community during the corresponding periods?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware that both Muslim and Croat communities had Crisis Staffs. I've also encountered the term "War Presidency" for some -- in some of those municipalities. I did not examine them for the purposes of this report nor have I ever been -- had an inquiry to respond to -- regarding those -- in those terms there are other members of the team who deal with the structures of the Bosnian Muslim forces and the Bosnian Croat forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But you are well aware, are you, that significant actions were also being taken by the other relations for these purposes, but that's -- if I leave Croats on one side certainly because the significance of the Muslims in this matter is rather greater for our purposes, but that significant actions were being taken by the Muslim community in relation to Crisis Staffs, in relation to preparations which might be defensive in some circumstances, might be aggressive in other circumstances, towards the end of 1991 and early 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will certainly agree that there were Crisis Staffs as I said on both the Muslim and the Croat side, and I would like not to leave the Croats aside simply because I see that term used more -- I'm more aware of the term "Crisis Staff" used among the Croats, not -- I certainly see it -- I believe that there were municipal Crisis Staffs that involved both Muslims and Croats in more mixed municipalities, or more specifically ethnic -- so I agree there were Muslim Crisis Staffs. I simply -- as a term "Crisis Staff" as opposed to "War Presidency," I see that more among the Croats which is why I'm not going to put it aside entirely. As for the actual actions they have -- they took at this time period, I did not look into those actions specifically, and I have no basis for comparing what they did with the actions of those Crisis Staffs which I did look at, the Bosnian Serb Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, the -- December 1991 and just -- let's assume for the moment that this document was disseminated in the way that you have concluded to the people, to whom it went, and so on. Nobody in December 1991, the Serbs, the Muslims, the Croats, heard -- nobody knew what was going to happen over the next few months, did they? Nobody knew whether there was going to be widespread war in Bosnia and Herzegovina or whether, with a bit of hope, that might be avoided?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did happen was the result of choices people made. People on the ground didn't know -- no one can know the future, but people can have plans and make decisions and take steps. So the future -- the events that happened were not blind forces but the result of choices made on all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This -- I'm going to try and short circuit this as much as possible. This particular document, Ms. Hanson, does simply not, in its own terms, it does not imply the division of Bosnia and Herzegovina along ethnic lines?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It implies the division of municipalities along ethnic lines and it is to be implemented throughout Bosnia. And in understanding the document, one has to look at what the people involved said about the document and how they referred to it and how they treated it. And I've indicated that in my presentation, the references that even -- Karadzic says taking over real functions. It was a plan for action, and those actions were taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, do you say that the actions -- actions were taken anywhere in accordance with this document, item by item, and implementing the whole list of instructions contained in this document? Do you -- can you -- can you identify a single municipality that carried out 80 per cent of the items in this document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't put a figure on it, but if you look at the Novo Sarajevo receipt of that document and their implementation, they assign people to a good number of the tasks as specified in there. Of course, the available evidence does not allow me to make one -- make a checklist that every municipality carried out -- or any municipality did every single thing. We don't have a record -- a document -- a record that would indicate that, but we see a consistent pattern of the main steps being implemented on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you agree that -- well, no, let's put it another way. Where the Serbs are in majority in a municipality, what, from your reading of the documents, do you suggest was the point of variant A?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: To take over all organs of authority, to have the Serbian police, because even in Serb majority municipalities, non-Serbs were in the municipal organs generally in proportion to the representation in the population, or at least in proportion to the results of the election, which, as we know, generally went to the national parties. So not all municipal positions would be held by Serbs or SDS members, and variant A is making sure that those are the SDS members who have those positions in a parallel government, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So what you're -- what you're saying is that it was -- it was more productive and it was a better plan to have a parallel government than to use your effective political control of the existing government?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was better, but that is the choice made in this document as I read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let's look at what Dr. Karadzic said at the 50th Republika Srpska Assembly, which we find in master binder 2, at tab 49.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I can tell you what -- I can tell you what I'm looking for, Ms. Hanson. I'm looking for where Dr. Karadzic refers to A and B.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- you have dealt with --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have it on the ELMO. It's page 323 of the English translation, and in the B/C/S, it's 00846058.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: "At the moment --" thank you. "At the moment the war began in the municipalities where we were in the majority," that's just over halfway down the page, "we had municipal power, held it firmly, controlled everything. In the municipalities where we were in the minority, we set up secret government, Municipal Boards, Municipal Assemblies, presidents of Executive Boards. You will remember the A and B variants. In the B variant, where we were in the minority, 20 per cent, 15 per cent, we had set up a government and a brigade, a unit, no matter what size, but there was a detachment with a commander." That last bit in the B variant, "we have set up a government and a brigade, a unit, a detachment with a commander," that doesn't fit the content of that document in variant B, does it, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They speak of mobilising the reserve police and the TO. And as I explained in some municipalities, the SDS and the Crisis Staffs did form TO units. It's not an express statement. The brigade, unit, detachment with a commander as such is not specified in the 19th December instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Are you aware from your reading of the papers that by the time it got to 1995, which this was, that there was, in effect, a dispute between the civilian leaders, Dr. Karadzic, and the military leaders, in effect, as to what had gone wrong?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of a conflict. The substance of the conflict I'm not sure of, but I certainly agree there was a conflict between civilian and military authorities, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And there was -- there was a considerable amount of -- or there were a considerable amount of claims being made on both sides about how much they had done for the Serb cause?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not aware of the substance of the conflict between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That the -- you're not even aware that there was -- there was that tenor of the debate at that time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- as I say, I have not referred to any -- I have not looked specifically at any of the speeches and debates about that. It's -- it seems consistent, but I am not going to answer with any confidence that I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And it's your inference that Dr. Karadzic is referring to the same documents that we've been looking at, the instructions from December 1991, variants A and B, as they've come to be known?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my inference.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: What was the -- how do you fit together, then, the instructions for operation of Crisis Staffs which were issued by the government under Mr. Djeric on the 26th of April, 1992? Why were those necessary at that time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because at that time in many municipalities, Crisis Staffs had come out of secret and had declared themselves to be the municipal governments and to be part of the Bosnian Serb state. And these are instructions from the government on how they are to operate in the Bosnian Serb state. We saw in the Assembly request from Vjestica and others, Give us instructions, and Djeric saying, Don't take actions into your own hands, you will get instructions. I tie all those together as part of the evolution of the Bosnian Serb state and definition of role of Crisis Staffs in that state.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your thesis is that they already had those instructions back in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had one set of instructions. They had the 19 December instructions, but they were asking, as we saw in the municipality -- in the Assembly minutes, for more and they received more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The instructions of December are far more detailed than the instructions given later, weren't they, assuming they were given?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do assume they were given, as I've indicated in my presentation. They are more specific about some matters about specific steps to be taken in the municipal level. Djeric's instructions speak more to the general functions of the Crisis Staff and their role in the state. There is one thing rather specific in Djeric's instructions that -- on the question of moving artillery and controlling the use of artillery seized in war operations. That seems quite specific. But on the whole, it does not have the same itemised list that we see in the 19 December instructions. It does itemise what are to be the tasks of the members of the Crisis Staff, and as I indicated in my presentation, they generally correspond to the taskings of the 19 December instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Hannis, is there any need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did have some areas that I wanted to address --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- if I may. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, I want to direct you to the topic of the July Presidency session where there was the discussion about Mr. Koljevic requesting to step down and the reason he gave was of his perceived failure to control the republican commissioners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, this was from the 7th of March, and at page 81 of the transcript where that discussion begins.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you take that comment by him to indicate that he was the only member of the Presidency that had up to that time sole responsibility for the war commissioners?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see that -- such a specific reference in his speech. He just is -- seems to be listing the things that aren't going well and the problems he's facing, but he does not seem to be claiming sole responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In connection with that I would like to show you a document that was not in the presentation but is in your master binder at master tab 169. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I misspoke. This is in Mr. Treanor's binder. This was an exhibit that came through him in P65, and it's at master tab 169. We've made copies of this just to hand around now so we don't have to go find Mr. Treanor's binders. And the ERN of the B/C/S I think is 0076-7932, and the English is 0081-4294 through 95.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you have a copy of that document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if I'm correct, this is a Presidency session on the 25th of June, 1992, a couple of weeks before the one where Mr. Koljevic is asking to be relieved.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you have a look there and tell us -- I think there's a reference to Mr. Koljevic actually being assigned to a particular duty in connection with commissioners.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's the last item of the minutes, and it says that Dr. Koljevic is charged with appointing commissioners of the Serbian municipality of Sarajevo centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you know did Mr. -- did Dr. Koljevic have any particular relationship with the Sarajevo centre municipality in terms of where he lived, where he was from, or where he had family?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he was from Sarajevo. I don't know that it was the centre municipality per se, but he was from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, if he had had complete responsibility for all matters relating to commissioners, would it have been necessary to make a specific designation for him to appoint a commissioner?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't seem logical, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in that document, was there some reference to the issue that comes up later on in July - I think raised by Branko Djeric - about assigning or dividing responsibilities among the various members of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The item immediately above the item I just read, top of the translation, page 2, that working bodies of the Presidency be set up and authority and responsibilities be precisely divided among the members of the Presidency would appear to relate directly to that division of labour -- of tasks that we see at the Presidency session in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So it appears that this is still an issue that hasn't been resolved?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That's how it appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now I want to go to presentation tab 122. I don't know if we need to get the whole thing. This was the discussion of the Assembly session where there was discussion about the commissioner -- the war commissioners. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we should give it to you.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's several long speeches, Krajisnik and Maksimovic, and Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And what I wanted to ask you about was Mr. Krajisnik's speech where he mentioned the commissioners with whom he had personally had dealings and was aware of what they had been doing, if you can find that.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the English translation it's page 104. The speech begins on the previous page, but page 104. I think the relevant section -- and in the B/C/S 02149731.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, what I'm interested in, this relates to the issue of what information Mr. Krajisnik might have had in terms of reports about what was happening in various municipalities. Can you tell us which commissioners he mentions by name as the ones that he dealt with?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko -- he says about each one of our members. He says: "I was informed about each one of our members." Then he names Mirko Mijatovic, Jovo Mijatovic, Cancar, Marko Simic, Branko Simic, and Vojo Maksimovic. Cancar I take to be Petar Cancar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who was from where? If you remember.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Foca, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, we've seen in your presentation some documents concerning appointments of some of those commissioners, and just to save a little time, if it's all right with Defence counsel, I want to mention some of those individuals and what documents they appear in. Jovo Mijatovic was in presentation tab 75 which was one of the ones that Mr. Krajisnik has signed and he was appointed for Ilijas; Marko Simic was appointed for Stari Grad in presentation tab 74; and Vojo Maksimovic was in presentation tab 67 for Foca. Now, I want to ask you about presentation tab 69 which was the June 16th appointment of Dragan Jovanovic. Do you have that in the binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think that's in presentation binder number 2. This is another one that we have an indication from Defence counsel that appears to be Mr. Krajisnik's signature based on his viewing of the Xerox copy. Can you tell us the date of that appointment?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th of June, 1992, appointing Dragan Jovanovic as republican commissioner for Ilijas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he replaces somebody?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovan Tintor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what has happened to Mr. Tintor according to that document?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's been transferred to a new position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So this was June 16th, 1992, after Mr. Krajisnik was a member of the expanded Presidency?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And before the July 10th session where there was discussion about dividing up the duties and making him responsible -- or making him the point of contact for matters relating to commissioners?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: With regard to signatures, we've seen on other documents sometimes when it is not signed by the person whose typewritten signature appears that the word "za" appears in B/C/S. Can you tell us what that means?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Za" means "for," and therefore he is -- in this context it means signing for the type-signed name.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: These three documents that have Mr. Krajisnik's signature for the appointments, did you see the word "za" on any of them?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That does not appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I want to move on to the discussion about a document from Zivinice, if you can understand my pronunciation. Zivinice. That was the SDS and a "Crisis Staff" dealing with the issue of roadblocks. Judge Orie asked you a question about the nature of that Crisis Staff and asked you -- I think the phrase he used was it conceivable that maybe that was a Crisis Staff that had a retarded start or a late start?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall telling us about Mr. Karadzic speaking in the March 1992 Assembly session and telling the deputies to go home and form Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He says "urgently in those where you have not yet formed them," I believe he says.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So if there's not a Crisis Staff in Zivinice in February 1992, that's not inconsistent with what Mr. Krajisnik is saying in March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I take it that statement of Karadzic's to read that in fact not all municipalities had formed a Crisis Staff by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me move on to another topic dealing with reporting by Crisis Staffs up to the higher levels of authority. Do you recall the discussion pertaining to the Stari Grad municipality? There was a report from them about -- requesting an investigation of somebody in a particular business and appointing somebody else as the acting director.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall the discussion about that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Stewart asked you a question about the significance of that report, and this was in May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: According to the instructions from the government in late April of 1992 from Branko Djeric about the operation of Crisis Staffs, was there a reporting requirement in those instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a reporting requirement to the central and regional state organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
