utterances.text: And relating to those questions, one of the last things that Mr. Stewart asked you was about the Variant A and B instructions on the one hand and the April 1992 instructions from the government. One of the differences has to do with the timing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came out at very different times in the development of the Bosnian Serb state.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in terms of take-overs of municipalities, had take-overs occurred before December of 1991?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And after April 24th or 26th of 1992, had take-overs occurred?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One of the questions also related to contacts between the accused, Mr. Krajisnik, and local Crisis Staffs or representatives of local Crisis Staffs. Now, I'm not sure if this was in your presentation. You did talk about Kljuc municipality and the diary of Mr. Bajic who kept minutes of the Crisis Staffs. Do you recall mention in that document of a February 5th, 1992, meeting in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And did that involve a meeting between Mr. Krajisnik, Mr. Karadzic, and representatives of local and regional Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is a minor point, but I want to take you to the intercept, the phone conversation between Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Tintor where -- I think we can do it without the document. You were asked about whether this was just a personal contact or a business contact. This is the one where Mr. Tintor indicated he thought it was his duty to inform Mr. Krajisnik of certain matters.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you mentioned that he -- Mr. Tintor asked for the Speaker when he first got on the line.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And there's the obvious point that the call is being made to his office and it would be natural to ask for the Speaker. Do you recall that there was -- in the conversation Mr. Tintor apparently speaking to people at his end of the phone about who he was speaking with?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he says the president -- I believe the words "predzjednik." But in terms of presiding, without it right in front of me, I think that's a reading of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's fine. I can refer the Judges to that document to see. I want to ask you about a question Judge Hanoteau asked you concerning the reference in the Assembly about the MPs or the deputies transferring authority of the Assembly to the municipalities. I think Judge Hanoteau asked you the question about: Wasn't this a democratic government at the time? I guess that's my question. Is this a democratic government in the terms that you or I might think of of a Western-type democracy?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I pointed out, these deputies were not elected to this body. They left the body to which they had been elected and formed their own and assigned it authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And with regard to the authorities in the municipality, and the Crisis Staffs in the local municipalities, in Variant A municipalities, some of those people had been elected to the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But in the Variant B municipality, was that the case?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fewer would have been -- generally the sharing out of municipal positions was done along the lines of the local election results, so it generally reflected the ethnic makeup, so there would be some SDS people and some municipal positions in Variant B municipality, but fewer -- many fewer than in Variant A.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In fact the Crisis Staffs were not the officially elected representatives but was rather a body to deal with the emergency situation?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Who had the power to appoint or dismiss members of Crisis Staffs in municipalities? And I'm talking about SDS Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The appointment is done through the instructions of -- from the Main Board, the 19 December instructions, through Djeric's instructions, naming who is going on to a Crisis Staff. There's no discussion of who has the power to dismiss them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I want to take you to two other points quickly, and then I thing I'll be finished. Ratko Adzic, do you know what his position was before the war?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess we'll wait for some further information from the Defence. Do you know he was elected mayor of the municipality and was not a member of the JNA at that time?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That jogs with my general understanding that he was as president -- became president of the Crisis Staff because he was president of the municipality. Yes, that's my general understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The document that we looked at where he is saying that as a commander that was addressed to the Presidency, making a request for certain --

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tanks --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- certain military matters, within the VRS and in the JNA, would it be typical for a military commander to address the Presidency directly as opposed to his own commander or the Main Staff of the army?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not be typical. One would expect an address via army channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And finally with regard to the Variant A and Variant B instructions, Mr. Stewart asked you the question about, did you find it odd that the cover page said Main Board and the typed signature page said SDS Crisis Staff. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And he talked to you about the dearth of evidence of an SDS republic level Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you find that odd or consistent with trying to set up a secret government?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's entirely consistent with trying to set up a secret government.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, am I wrong when I assume that you would have further questions for Ms. Hanson on the basis of re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no further questions --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't put on my microphone. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am a bit in doubt what to do at this moment. I would have to go through my notes again to see whether I would have any additional questions. I'm just informed that my fellow Judges would most likely have no further questions. Would it be possible, Ms. Hanson, to remain, stand by, and follow instructions even when it's not certain that we'd have further questions for you. We'd of course, then, immediately let you know if there are any further questions. If, however, there would be any further questions, we would like to see you back tomorrow morning. It will certainly not take much time, because if I have any questions, it's mainly in terms of clarifying issues. Therefore, I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony you have given, neither about the testimony you may be about to give, and to remain on stand-by for tomorrow morning. If we'll not call you back anymore, I would already like to thank you for -- well, not having come a far distance, but at least having come and answered many questions of the parties and of the Bench until now. But it might be that there are two or three more. Mr. Hannis, this also means that even if there would be further questions for Ms. Hanson tomorrow, that it certainly will not take long and that you should be prepared to call your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger will be ready. If you could advise us before the end of the day, then the appropriate one of us will show up at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until tomorrow, same courtroom, 9.00. And we might see you back tomorrow morning, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
